question.text: If there is no nominee registered for a deceased unitholder's mutual fund investments, how does the transmission process work across different value thresholds?

answer.text: The AMC distributes the units equally among all family members regardless of value

The documentation requirement depends on the value of the folio: for smaller folios (up to Rs.5 lakhs) legal heirs can proceed with the death certificate, evidence of relationship, indemnity, affidavits and a NOC from other heirs; for higher-value folios (above Rs.10 lakhs) legal representation such as a probated will, succession certificate, or letter of administration/court decree is required
The units become part of the unclaimed amounts pool
The units are automatically transferred to the spouse

explanation.text: The Logic: For no-nominee transmission, the workbook prescribes a threshold-based document process. Up to Rs.5 lakhs per folio, the legal heir(s) can typically proceed with the death certificate, KYC, evidence of relationship, indemnity bond/affidavit and a NOC from other legal heirs, without requiring legal representation. Above Rs.10 lakhs, legal representation such as a probated will, succession certificate, or letter of administration / court decree is generally required. This makes nominee registration a strong simplifier. The Trap: There is no automatic transfer to a spouse, no equal distribution rule, and the units do not become unclaimed merely because a nominee was not registered. Treating the documentation as a single universal list also misses the threshold-based design. Note: AMCs and RTAs apply the value threshold per folio and may require additional indemnities or NOCs based on the facts. The intermediate band between the two thresholds is treated case-by-case based on the documents the heir can produce.
